Class LostCases

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.curriculum.LostCases
public final class LostCases extends Object
The fights it lost, kept to be fought again until it wins them. A scripted opponent is drawn anew for every fight: its reactions, its aim, its rhythm, how it crits, its connection, how far a hit moves it. A fight in which the fighter took more damage than it dealt is an opponent, so drawn, that beats it, and very likely the very pattern a person who finds it would beat it with too. So it is kept exactly as it was set up, down to the seed its chances were drawn from (where the two start, every choice the bot makes), and a share of the fights against that stage's opponents are those kept ones again (Config.replayLostShare), the worst first, each a few times running, from the same start, until each has been won twice in a row. Then it is beaten, and kept apart: once none of a stage's lost fights are left, the beaten ones are fought again in turn, since a fight won twice can still be forgotten; one lost again goes back on the list. In training terms: prioritised replay of the levels it fails, each level replayed from its seed.

The user, 19 October: "make it train on the exact same case on those it still didnt beat yet more more more ... until all the cases are win ... there is a very high chance that is the exact round my friend finds to beat this". And at 22:10: once it has learned all of them, "let it learn all the cases again and find cases it loses". 20 October: "replicate those cases it failed 1-1 from start so like it actually learns it", and no fighting the ones it has won meanwhile.

Plain bookkeeping and the draw; the trainer sets the fights up and saves the list.

  • Field Details

    • MOST

      public static final int MOST
      At most this many are kept; past that a parked one makes room, else the mildest loss. 400 left each one fought again only every two hours or so (20 October).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • PARK_REPLAYS

      public static final int PARK_REPLAYS
      Fought again this many times and never won: parked (12 since replays became exact and run three at a time, 20 October). It stays on the list, but comes up a tenth as often, last as the one waited longest, and first to make room. On 19-20 October fights it could not win (no-knockback 246 replays and none won) took the replays, and it learned to give up against the hardest kinds: less damage dealt to the spacer and the punisher in the frozen test.

    • STALEST_SHARE

      static final float STALEST_SHARE
      This share of the picks is the kept fight picked longest ago, so that every one gets its turn; the rest go by how badly it was lost. Without it a few fights lost by 250-300 a minute took most of the replays while others waited (19 October). Prioritised level replay mixes in staleness the same way.

    • byPotential

      public boolean byPotential
      Prioritised level replay (Jiang, Grefenstette and Rocktaschel, ICML 2021): the kept fights are drawn by how much fighting them last taught (LostCases.Case.potential, the mean |GAE| of its steps), rank by rank, the k-th weighing 1/k, instead of by how badly they were lost. Up to 21 October the worst losses came first, and only 1 to 13 of about 85 replays in half an hour were won: the worst-lost fights are mostly the ones there is least to learn from yet. One never scored comes first (it has not been tried), the one picked longest ago first among equals. Set from Config.replayByPotential.
